title: What happens in puberty?
intro: Puberty is the time when a child's body changes into an adult body and becomes capable of reproduction. It is driven by hormones and brings physical, emotional and social changes. The timing varies between young people, and this is normal.

sections.heading: What starts puberty
paragraphs: Puberty begins when the brain signals the pituitary gland to release hormones that stimulate the ovaries or testicles. In girls this usually starts between about eight and thirteen years, and in boys between nine and fourteen. Genes, nutrition, weight and general health influence timing.

sections.heading: Changes in girls
paragraphs: Breast development is usually the first sign, followed by pubic and underarm hair, a growth spurt, wider hips and, about two years after breast growth begins, the first period. Periods may be irregular at first. Skin may become oilier and acne can appear.

sections.heading: Changes in boys
paragraphs: The testicles and scrotum enlarge first, followed by growth of the penis, pubic and body hair, a growth spurt, deepening of the voice and facial hair. Erections and night-time ejaculations (wet dreams) are normal. Acne and sweating increase. Muscles become stronger.

sections.heading: Emotional and social changes
paragraphs: Young people may have mood swings, stronger feelings, need for privacy, more interest in relationships and worries about body image. The brain also continues to develop, especially in areas of judgement and impulse control. Sleep needs increase. Support, clear information and respect help.

sections.heading: When to seek advice
paragraphs: See a doctor if signs begin before eight in girls or nine in boys, if there is no sign by thirteen in girls or fourteen in boys, if periods have not started by sixteen, or for severe pain, heavy bleeding, severe acne or worries about mood. Talk openly about hygiene, consent, safe sex and body changes.

examples.title: Talking at home
examples.text: Imagine your child asks about periods or wet dreams. You could answer calmly and honestly, and offer a good book or website.

examples.title: Noticing early signs
examples.text: Suppose your daughter develops breasts at seven. You might arrange a check with the paediatrician.
